headline: Malaysia's Respond.io raises $62.5M Series B for its AI agent-powered messaging app
summary: The Kuala Lumpur-based startup, which leverages AI agents for customer conversations across multiple channels, has grown to $35M ARR with a 30% profit margin and plans strategic acquisitions.
details: Respond.io, a Malaysian startup focused on customer conversation management, has successfully raised a $62.5 million Series B funding round. The investment was led by Camber Partners, with additional participation from Endeavor Catalyst and existing investors. The company last secured a $7 million Series A in 2022.

The platform has achieved $35 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR), demonstrating a 169% year-over-year growth rate, alongside a 30% profit margin. Respond.io helps mid- to large-sized B2C businesses manage customer interactions across various messaging apps like WhatsApp, Instagram, and TikTok.

Founded in 2017 by Gerardo Salandra, Hassan Ahmed, and Iaroslav Kudritskiy, Respond.io utilizes AI agents to automate high volumes of customer inquiries. These agents are capable of qualifying leads and closing sales without requiring human intervention.

CEO Gerardo Salandra highlights that their core customers are in 'high-consideration' sectors such as healthcare, automotive, and travel, where direct customer interaction is crucial before a purchase. The platform is ideally suited for companies employing between 200 and 10,000 people.

The company currently processes 2 billion messages per quarter and attributes its accelerated growth to the increasing prominence of AI. Unlike many enterprise software competitors, Respond.io charges based on the volume of customer conversations, rather than per seat, which aligns well with AI-driven efficiency.

With the new capital, Respond.io plans to expand its team, pursue organic growth, and strategically acquire other companies. The CEO is targeting both bolt-on technologies that complement their existing ecosystem and established teams with strong customer bases in key markets.

Respond.io currently generates approximately 30% of its revenue from APAC, 30% from Latin America, and 20% from the Middle East and Africa. North America and Western Europe, which currently account for 20%, are identified as the fastest-growing regions and are projected to become the largest segments within two to three years.

headline_marked: [[FIFA World Cup 2026 streaming panel exposed]] to unauthorized control
headline: FIFA World Cup 2026 streaming panel exposed to unauthorized control
summary: A security researcher found that FIFA's agent registration platform granted access to the live production streaming management panel for the 2026 World Cup, allowing potential hijacking of live feeds.
details: A security researcher gained access to the live production Streaming Management panel for the FIFA World Cup 2026, including controls for every match and camera angle. This was possible through a vulnerability in FIFA's agent registration platform.

The flaw stemmed from FIFA adding agent accounts to their Microsoft Entra tenant, which powers all internal platforms. While client-side checks denied access, backend APIs did not verify roles, allowing unauthorized access to critical systems.

The exposed panel provided full control over streaming, including start, stop, and schedule functions for all matches and camera feeds. It also revealed RTMP ingest URLs and stream keys, which could be used to replace live camera feeds.

An attacker could have pushed their own video content, like a "Rickroll" or "Subway Surfers" gameplay, to replace the main broadcast output (PGM feed) on every TV network worldwide during an active match. The researcher confirmed live tactical camera feeds were accessible via preview URLs.

Beyond streaming controls, the "NO_ROLES" account also accessed other sensitive platforms, including Competitions, Matches, Teams, Analysis Dashboard, and a live match dashboard with real-time event timelines. The researcher reported the vulnerability to FIFA, MediaKind, HBS, CISA, and the FBI.
caption:
